points.description: States the purpose: both are broadcast mechanisms that are more efficient than plain flooding, i.e. they reduce/minimize duplicate packets in the network when broadcasting.

Reverse Path Forwarding: a node X receiving a packet from source S via neighbor N checks its unicast routing table and forwards the packet to all other neighbors (not N) only if N is the next hop X would use to send to S (packet arrived on the best/shortest path); otherwise it discards it.

levels.says: Mentions only the check against the routing table / forwarding only if arrived on the best path to the source, without saying it is forwarded to all neighbors except the incoming one (or vice versa).

points.description: Reverse Path Broadcast: works like RPF, but nodes learn (e.g. by observing unicast traffic) which edges are part of a spanning tree/best paths, and forward only on those tree edges (excluding the incoming link), reducing duplicates further.

levels.says: Says it is like RPF but restricted to spanning-tree edges, without explaining how the tree edges are learned, or the reverse.

rubric.notes: Full marks need purpose (fewer duplicates than flooding), RPF mechanism (forward only if packet came from the neighbor on the best route back to the source), and RPB mechanism (RPF restricted to spanning-tree edges learned from unicast traffic). Part marks for incomplete mechanism descriptions. No marks for describing them as plain flooding or unrelated algorithms.
